StackType.issue: Closed 2026-07-30 (tier-2 campaign): (Task 25.) The 15 `on_stack` no-op overrides are DELETED; the base `Power.on_stack` adds, matching PowerCmd.ModifyAmount (PowerCmd.cs:236), which adds unconditionally with no StackType branch -- PowerStackType.Single means 'Amount is hidden and displayed as 1' (PowerStackType.cs:10-13), not 'does not stack'. All 16 units re-verified against their own C#: 15 are StackType.Single, and NONE overrides InstanceType (PowerModel.cs:144 default None), so none needs T1's instance machinery instead of amount-adding. Two per-site exceptions, both verified: (1) DAMPEN's C# StackType is actually `None`, not Single (DampenPower.cs:22) -- the queue's 16-unit list was wrong about it; its only applier, MagiKnight, dedupes caller-side (MagiKnight.cs:78-96: re-application calls AddCaster only and never reaches PowerCmd.Apply), so the deletion is inert through the real caller and T28's caster-set machinery is untouched and re-pinned. (2) HEX genuinely reads Amount (HexPower.cs:79 feeds CardCmd.Afflict<Hexed>(card, Amount)), so this deletion closes a real divergence that remains DORMANT only because SpectralKnight's move machine never loops back to HEX and KnightsElite fields exactly one -- a second Hex applier makes it live. ILLUSION needed no override and is unchanged (the opposite-sign case the record notes). No reachable re-application among the other 13: Burrowed and Soar re-apply only after their own expire/remove, always onto a fresh instance. Pins: test/test_stack_type_single.py (39 tests).  The text it replaced read: PowerStackType.Single with the sim's on_stack overridden to `pass` -- the settled census's 15-unit wrong-reasoning class (`py audit/tools/power_census.py stack`); PowerCmd.ModifyAmount (PowerCmd.cs:236) adds unconditionally. DORMANT: Surrounded's behaviour is driven entirely by the private `_facing`/`self.facing` state (SurroundedPower.cs:27, powers.py:2547) and NOTHING reads Amount on either side; and the only ported applier, monsters/hive/kaiser_crab.py:112-114, applies it exactly once, guarded by `if combat is not None`, when the Rocket arm is constructed (Rocket.cs:93). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

ModifyDamageMultiplicative.issue: The arithmetic and the facing logic are exact -- `dealer == null -> 1m`, `target != base.Owner -> 1m`, then 1.5x only if the dealer holds the marker power OPPOSITE the facing (SurroundedPower.cs:46-72 vs powers.py:2559-2565), and 1.5 is dyadic so hook_dispatch G9 does not bite (`power_census.py multipliers`). The gap is that this is one of only NINE C# Modify{Damage,Block}{Additive,Multiplicative} overrides that do NOT self-gate on powered-ness (executed: `py audit/tools/power_slot_probes.py ungated-modifiers`, 37 gated / 9 ungated), while the sim gates the WHOLE dispatch at the pipeline level (cmds.py:56-58, `if is_powered_attack(props)`). So an Unpowered but dealer-attributed hit on a Surrounded player gets 1.5x in the game and 1.0x in the sim. `damage_pipeline` gap G3 already owns this mechanism AND already names SurroundedPower by name as its example, so the verdict is carried unchanged here per rule 3. DORMANT, verified rather than inherited: the multiplier needs a dealer holding BackAttackLeft/RightPower, and the only two such creatures anywhere are the Kaiser Crab arms (Crusher.cs:117, Rocket.cs:94; sim kaiser_crab.py:46,115), whose every damage source is an AttackIntent -- a grep of Crusher.cs and Rocket.cs for `Unpowered`/`Unblockable` returns nothing, and the sim's arms only ever call `_execute_attack` (kaiser_crab.py:76-97, 141-153). Trigger: any unpowered damage dealt BY a Kaiser Crab arm, or porting HangPower / ShadowmeldPower (the two other ungated power overrides, both unported). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

BeforeCardPlayed.rationale: SurroundedPower.cs:74-80 flips facing on any TARGETED card play by the owner's player, damaging or not; powers.py:2573-2578 does the same on `target is not None`, and its comment correctly argues `cardPlay.Card.Owner == base.Owner.Player` is a single-player tautology (Surrounded only ever lands on the player). test/test_hive.py:957-983 pins the targeted-Skill case.

BeforePotionUsed.maps_to: powers.py:2580-2582 on_potion_used -- but that is the sim's AfterPotionUsed slot (hooks.py:566-571, combat.py:610), NOT BeforePotionUsed, which the sim never dispatches
BeforePotionUsed.issue: Closed 2026-07-27: the sim's single potion dispatch was split in two. `hooks.before_potion_used` (hooks.py:779-790) is fired at combat.py:736 BEFORE `potion.use` (:737) and `on_potion_used` after it (:738), mirroring PotionModel.OnUseWrapper (PotionModel.cs:293 RemoveBeforeUse, :297 BeforePotionUsed, :327 OnUse, :338 AfterPotionUsed); SurroundedPower now implements `before_potion_used` (powers.py:2741-2745) and Belt Buckle / Reptile Trinket stay on the after slot. VERIFIED 2026-07-27 by reading hooks.py, combat.py:725-740 and powers.py. WAS: the facing flip ran one phase late, so a potion that killed its target re-faced on the corpse -- worth 1.5x damage on the next hit.

AfterDeath.issue: The logic matches SurroundedPower.cs:90-100 -- skip when the dead creature is on the owner's own side, then, if every remaining hittable enemy carries the SAME marker power, re-face on hittableEnemies[0] -- but the sim reads `[e for e in combat.enemies if not e.is_gone]` (powers.py:2590) where C# reads `base.Owner.CombatState.HittableEnemies`. Recurring gap shape 7: HittableEnemies applies Hook.ShouldAllowHitting, so a creature the game refuses to hit (a mid-revival Decimillipede segment, an Illusion/Adaptable/Reattach holder in its un-hittable window) is counted by the sim and not by the game, which can flip the `all(...)` test and hence the facing -- and facing is worth 1.5x damage. C#'s `wasRemovalPrevented` early-out is separately dropped by the sim (see the guard below). DORMANT: the Kaiser Crab boss is exactly the two arms (monsters/hive/kaiser_crab.py:159-162), neither of which overrides ShouldAllowHitting, so `not is_gone` and HittableEnemies agree for every creature that can ever be in this power's combat. Trigger: an encounter that puts a Kaiser Crab arm alongside an Illusion / Adaptable / Reattach holder, all three of which are ported powers. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

guards.issue: Absent from powers.py:2584-2586, which tests only the side. C# skips the re-facing entirely when a death's REMOVAL was prevented (the creature is still there, so the board did not change); the sim re-runs its `all(...)` scan anyway. Folded into the AfterDeath entry's rollup and dormant by the same argument -- no ported creature in a Kaiser Crab combat prevents its own removal -- but it survives an is_gone-vs-HittableEnemies fix, so it is carried on its own.

guards.rationale: `Direction.Right` is the zero value of the enum (SurroundedPower.cs:19-23) and powers.py:2547 initialises `self.facing = "right"`. Checked rather than assumed because the whole power hangs on it.

Facing Right flips to Left only if the target has BackAttackLEFT, and vice versa (SurroundedPower.cs:104-118); powers.py:2567-2571 reproduces both arms including the `elif`, so a target with the marker matching the current facing does NOT flip. Easy to get backwards; it is right.
